paper_summary: This is a computational-mechanics methodology paper: it proposes a finite-element substructure (super-finite-element) technique for modelling metal matrix syntactic foams with reduced degrees of freedom, avoiding both homogenization and CT-based meshing while preserving the disordered interior structure. A two-dimensional 10 x 10 mm aluminium-matrix model containing iron hollow spheres (63% cavity space-filling, taken as the theoretical maximum gas fraction of MMSFs) is used only as a demonstration geometry. The reported results are purely numerical-performance metrics - memory utilization rate versus number of substructures, and running time of the conventional method versus the substructure technique (e.g. 99.95 s versus 31.71 s at 29282 DoF) - plus the optimal reduction ratios that minimize runtime.
extraction_notes: The paper's subject matter is metal matrix syntactic foams (aluminium matrix, iron hollow spheres), so it is topically adjacent, but it contains NO quantitative Process-Structure-Property data of any kind and therefore yields zero records. Specifically: no matrix or filler material constants are stated (no Young's modulus, Poisson ratio, density, strength, or yield stress for the aluminium, the iron hollow spheres, or the resulting foam); no foam was fabricated, so there is no processing route, no measured density, and no test condition; and no computed stiffness, strength, or displacement magnitudes are tabulated. Every number in the paper describes the numerical algorithm rather than the material: Table 1 gives memory usage rate versus number of substructures (4 -> 2.400 down to 100 -> 0.102, with an evident typo at 49 -> 0.010), Table 2 compares conventional-method and substructure-technique running times in seconds across 162-29282 DoF, and Table 3 lists reduction ratios (2.9 to 12.2) for minimum running time at 2738-502002 DoF. The only material-adjacent figures are geometric modelling assumptions: a 10 x 10 mm 2D model, 0.0125 mm mesh edge length, and a 63% spherical-cavity space-filling quoted from ref [7] (Marur, Materials Letters 2005) as the theoretical maximum gas percentage of MMSFs. That 63% is an assumed modelling parameter, not a measured or reported composition, and no property value is associated with it, so no 'model' record could be created for it either. is_syntactic_foam_paper was therefore set to false with an empty records list, per rule 10 ('no hollow-particle composite data'); note that this flag here means 'no extractable syntactic-foam data', not that the paper is about a different material class - it is a syntactic-foam modelling paper. This paper is a candidate for a separate 'methods/simulation, no data' category if the pipeline ever adds one. Figures 6-12 are plots without tabulated axis values and were not read.
